sections.heading: Our Process for Roof Inspection in Bloomfield, NJ

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing surveys the roof from the ground and the eaves first, then inspects every accessible surface on the roof, starting at the flashing details.

runs.v: Here is how a Bloomfield job runs: every roof call starts with a ground survey that photographs the roof planes and notes sagging ridgelines, missing shingles, staining, and moss, planning safe access per the InterNACHI standard of practice. Most Bloomfield inspections take about one hour.

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing examines the roof-covering materials, flashing at every penetration and transition, drainage, and sealants, and measures deck and framing moisture.

runs.v: The on-roof inspection checks shingles, valleys, gutters, pipe boots, ridge caps, and step flashing at roof-meets-wall joints, while moisture meters and infrared imaging locate trapped moisture before a ceiling stain appears; sealing the roof deck cuts water intrusion by up to 95%, per the IBHS.

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing delivers a written condition report with annotated photographs, a component-condition rating, an estimated remaining service-life range, and recommendations ranked by urgency.

runs.v: The result is a whole roof diagnosis, and written inspection reports serve homeowners and insurance claims: for a home sale the report assesses covering condition and active-leak indications per the InterNACHI standard of practice, and for a claim it records material, age, condition, and damage, the documentation a carrier accepts, per the Insurance Information Institute.

faqs.q: How often should you inspect a roof in Bloomfield, NJ?

runs.v: The NRCA recommends a roof inspection at least twice per year, spring and fall, plus one after any major weather event, so keep a Bloomfield repair calendar spring and fall. Maintenance on that cadence extends asphalt-shingle life by roughly 25–30%, per ARMA.

faqs.q: Can a roof inspection find a leak before it appears inside a Bloomfield home?

runs.v: Yes. Moisture meters and infrared imaging find trapped moisture in the deck, so a failing flashing or membrane detail is caught while a repair stays minor on Bloomfield's pre-war and two-family stock.

faqs.q: Do you inspect a tenant-occupied two-family or garden apartment in Bloomfield?

runs.v: Yes. Entry is coordinated with occupants under New Jersey landlord-tenant notice, and the owner receives timestamped photographs and a written condition report.
